correctness.rationale: Starting from the verified current and transfer-matrix expressions in arXiv:2606.01568v1, the positive stationary density parameter strictly increases with s. The exact current derivative has a quintic numerator whose coefficient list has exactly one sign change for each \(q>0\), proving one global maximum. The unique positive root has the nondegenerate scaling limit s/\(q^{-1/3}\) -> 2^(1/3), enabling two-order implicit-function expansions of vacancy and maximum current. The exactly simplified eigenvalue ratio gives the fixed-density correlation prefactor and the optimized correlation length. The packaged checker passed 67 symbolic and numerical assertion groups; numerical tests are corroboration, not the infinite proof. The same Markov two-point covariance geometric series yields the finite limiting susceptibility at the maximizing density.

originality.rationale: The founding paper gives stationary current and correlation eigenvalues but states only the fixed-density strong-recovery current limit and its general-density correlation-length coefficient. It does not identify the unique global density optimum, derive its \(q^{-1/3}\) boundary layer or second-order expansion, or obtain the optimized \(q^{1/3}\) clustering law. The stated fixed-density coefficient in its Eq. (19) does not follow from its own exact Eq. (18) except at \(\rho=1/2\). Distinct token-driven transport results provide comparisons but do not entail this stationary tandem model. The exact current and transfer-matrix formulas themselves are conceded as prior art; general implicit coverage remains a residual risk. The finite optimized susceptibility and its nontrivial compensation of diverging correlation length are included in the same singular asymptotic theorem.
residual_risks: The main paper supplies exact all-q/all-density current and transfer eigenvalues, so the new results are analytic consequences of these established formulas; a broader prior theorem might already contain their optimized consequences.
A strong-coupling nearest-neighbor Gibbs/Ising expansion may already imply the corrected fixed-density correlation coefficient; independent historical priority was not established.
Unindexed follow-up results on tandem transport may contain the same nonuniform boundary layer.
No independent review or external certification was performed.

value.rationale: The optimal current for strong recovery is controlled by a noncommuting high-density boundary layer; its vacancy fraction and transport defect share a sharp \(q^{-1/3}\) scale with explicit next-order constants. This directly quantifies throughput design and demonstrates that optimizing density changes cluster-size scaling from \(q^{1/2}\) at fixed density to \(q^{1/3}\). The correction of the published correlation prefactor has observable density dependence and, for example, changes the rho=1/5 leading prediction by a factor 2.5. The result is more than a single numerical example or a trivial fixed-parameter substitution. Despite a diverging optimal correlation length the integrated covariance tends to a finite universal value, a useful fluctuation-versus-correlation distinction.
